source.title: On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling
source.reading_method: Read the pinned local HTML directly, extracting mathematical alttext and surrounding prose with Python standard-library HTMLParser. No implementation, previous audit or generated topology informed these notes.

anchors_read.scope: Full orthogonal-group Haar probability and determinant-conditioned laws
Entire Appendix A.1 statement and proof, including Eq.12
B.2 introduction and standing measure/dimension conventions; direct introductory content only
Entire B.2.1 determinant-cancellation statement and proof, as the direct source input to B.2.2
Entire B.2.2, including Proposition B.7, Eqs.19-24 and the complete p6 lower-bound argument

notation_in_this_preread.s: sqrt(kappa), a nonnegative real square root; kappa >= 4 gives s >= 2
notation_in_this_preread.alpha: 1-1/n, with n viewed as a real in divisions and real powers

dimension_and_parameters: n is an integer block dimension. Section 3.1 has 3 <= n <= d; B.2 and Proposition B.7 use n >= 3 and kappa >= 4.
The B.2.2 single-block calculation does not need a block count k or an ambient d once the n-dimensional construction is fixed.
Section 3.1 chooses n=2T+1 only later for the main theorem, where T>=1 and 2T+1<=d. This choice is not an extra premise of the single-block Eq.24 calculation.
objects_domains_and_laws.full_haar: O(n)={O in R^(n x n): O^T O=I_n}, equipped with Haar probability. Each determinant component has probability 1/2. The bare expectations in B.2 are under this full-group Haar law.
objects_domains_and_laws.conditioned_haar: For b in {-1,+1}, mu_(n,b) is Haar probability conditioned on det(O)=b. It is a distinct law from the full-group Haar used in H and the spherical moments.

single_block_precision.gaussian: N(0,A_O^(-1)), with Lebesgue density p_O(x)=(2 pi)^(-n/2) sqrt(det A_O) exp(-x^T A_O x/2)
single_block_precision.source_bound_used_in_B22: I_n <= A_O <= kappa I_n in Loewner order

actual_single_block_mixture.sense: A mixture of probability laws: for a bounded measurable f, E_(X~P_b) f(X) = E_(O~mu_(n,b)) E_(X~N(0,A_O^(-1))) f(X). The precision varies with O inside the Gaussian law.
actual_single_block_mixture.density: p_b is the density of this actual mixture P_b. No replacement by a Gaussian with averaged precision or covariance is licensed by Section 3.1.

multi_block_context.law: For each fixed b, O_1,...,O_k are independent with common law mu_(n,b); their determinant signs are all b. D_b is the law of A_boldO.
multi_block_context.averaged_target: bar(pi)_b = E_(A~D_b) pi_A = P_b^(tensor k) tensor N(0,I_(d-kn))
multi_block_context.endpoint_convention: When kn=d, omit both the identity block and the final Gaussian factor.

objects_domains_and_laws.sphere_coordinate: In B.2, U=O_11. Since O e_1 is uniform on S^(n-1) under full Haar, U has the first-coordinate law of normalized surface probability on S^(n-1). It is not a determinant-conditioned coordinate law.

H_and_conditioned_test_gap.test_domain: For every lambda >= 0, h_lambda(x)=exp(-lambda ||x||^2) on R^n, with 0<h_lambda<=1.
H_and_conditioned_test_gap.H_definition: H(lambda)=E_(O~full Haar)[det(O) integral_(R^n) h_lambda(x) p_O(x) dx]
H_and_conditioned_test_gap.source_reason: The determinant components each have full Haar probability 1/2; det(O) is +1 or -1 on the corresponding component.
H_and_conditioned_test_gap.scope_warning: Eq.24 evaluates H itself. The signed conditioned test gap is twice that value; an absolute test gap or TV lower bound also removes the parity sign.

source_calculation_before_Eq23.conjugation: For every Q in O(n), conjugation preserves full Haar and determinant sign, A_(QOQ^T)=Q A_O Q^T, and p_(QOQ^T)(Qx)=p_O(x). Thus for every x, E[det(O)p_O(x)] = E[det(O)p_O(||x||e_1)]. This is a statement about the signed Haar average, not individual radiality of p_O.
source_calculation_before_Eq23.gaussian_integration: For a>0, integral_(R^n) exp(-a||x||^2/4) dx = (4 pi/a)^(n/2). Hence H(lambda)=2^(n/2) E[det(O) sqrt(det A_O) / (kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)U)^(n/2)].
source_calculation_before_Eq23.B6_input: Lemma B.6 is for every Borel h with E|h(U)|<infinity and says E[det(O)sqrt(det A_O)h(U)] = (-1)^(n-1)(s-1)^(n-1)/2^n times E[((s+1)U-(s-1))h(U)].
source_calculation_before_Eq23.zero_parameter_observation: At lambda=0, denominator matching would give r=q, but H(0)=0 since both target distributions have total mass one. The source therefore decreases r by the factor alpha.

selected_parameters_and_exact_values.strict_ranges: For every integer n>=3 and real kappa>=4, 0<r<1 and lambda>0. In particular 1-r^2>0 and n(n-1)>0.
selected_parameters_and_exact_values.selected_spherical_numerator_sign: Strictly negative on the source parameter range. This is a spherical expectation under the full-Haar coordinate law; it is not itself H(lambda) or a P_+1/P_-1 expectation difference.
selected_parameters_and_exact_values.powers_and_constants: n is the integer exponent in (-1)^n and q^n; n/2 in alpha^(n/2) and in kernel powers is the real half-dimension. The exact formula contains 1/n, 1/(1-r^2), and no omitted factor 2. All non-parity factors in the second line are strictly positive, so sign(H(lambda))=(-1)^n.
selected_parameters_and_exact_values.constant_scope: The selected r and lambda depend only on n and kappa. Eq.24 is an exact equality for that selection, not for arbitrary lambda>=0 or arbitrary 0<r<1. No unspecified constant or dependence on d, k, T or b occurs.

A1_two_moments_and_range.raw_dimension_wording: The statement begins 'Let n>=2' and later appends 'where n>=3' after identifying U as the first coordinate. Both clauses are present in the pinned source. This preread records the redundant/restrictive wording without silently broadening its advertised range.
A1_two_moments_and_range.consumer_dimension: B.2 uses n>=3 throughout, so the Eq.24 consumer is inside both dimension clauses.
A1_two_moments_and_range.law: zeta is uniform on S^(n-1); U=zeta_1; sigma is normalized surface measure.
A1_two_moments_and_range.proof_input: Poisson representation [5, Theorem 1.21] for every h harmonic on the unit ball and continuous on its closure: h(a)=integral h(u)(1-||a||^2)/||u-a||^n d sigma(u), ||a||<1. Apply at a=r e_1 to h(x)=1 and h(x)=x_1, using ||u-r e_1||^2=1+r^2-2r u_1, and divide by 1-r^2.
A1_two_moments_and_range.range_limits: These are weighted kernel moments with the same normalized law and same r. The displayed source does not assert r=1 or arbitrary real r. At the selected consumer r, the source has 0<r<1.
A1_two_moments_and_range.integrability_observation: For |U|<=1 and 0<r<1, 1+r^2-2rU >= (1-r)^2>0. The two kernel integrands and their fixed linear combination are bounded, hence integrable under normalized surface probability. This boundedness is an elementary reading check, not a claim of a compiled local lemma.

integrability_and_legality.explicit_source_domination: For lambda>=0 and every O,x, h_lambda(x) p_O(||x||e_1) <= (kappa/(2 pi))^(n/2) exp(-||x||^2/2). The source cites I_n<=A_O<=kappa I_n; with |det(O)|=1 this is the integrable bound used for Fubini.
integrability_and_legality.B6_h_integrability: The source chooses h(u)=(kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)u)^(-n/2). Since U in [-1,1], the denominator is at least 2+4lambda>0 for lambda>=0. Thus the Borel kernel is bounded on the coordinate support and satisfies B.6's E|h(U)|<infinity requirement.
integrability_and_legality.gaussian_legality: Positive precision and positive exponent coefficient justify the ordinary Gaussian integral. The full Haar law is a probability, and the determinant weight has absolute value one.
integrability_and_legality.binder_boundary: These integrability and positivity facts are discharged within the source calculation from its construction and parameter range. Source-facing production interfaces must not silently elevate the evaluated numerator, denominator matching, cancellation result, Fubini permission or desired conclusion into additional mathematical assumptions.

p6_dependencies: Convexity of t -> t^(n/2), using n/2>=1, gives alpha^(n/2)>=1/2.
Eq.20 and Eq.24 then yield TV(P_+1,P_-1) >= q^n/[2+4n s/(s+1)^2].
The denominator satisfies 2+4n s/(s+1)^2 <= 2+4n/s <= 2 exp(2n/s). Thus TV>=1/2 exp(-5n/s).
strict_scope: The Eq.24 exact equality and the selected spherical numerator value alone do not certify the p6 inequalities, the full Proposition B.7 TV bound, block amplification, Lemma 3.3, or the query-complexity theorem.
